title: Extended User Interrupts (xUI): Fast and Flexible Notification without Polling
problem: Intel's existing User Interrupt (UIPI) mechanism for fast user-space notification has correctness and performance limitations that prevent it from matching shared-memory polling latency while maintaining the efficiency of asynchronous notification. Current designs lack support for preemption in user-level runtimes, kernel-bypass timers, and efficient interrupt forwarding to accelerators.
motivation: High-performance systems (user-level runtimes, networking stacks, streaming accelerators) need notification mechanisms that avoid expensive kernel transitions but also avoid burning CPU cycles on polling; existing user-interrupt designs leave a performance gap.
method: xUI extends Intel's UIPI model with four hardware mechanisms: (1) tracked interrupts that allow senders to know when an interrupt was delivered, (2) hardware safepoints that let user-level runtimes implement preemption without kernel involvement, (3) a kernel-bypass timer for deadline-driven scheduling, and (4) interrupt forwarding to route notifications directly to accelerators (modeled on Intel's DSA). The design is modeled and evaluated in gem5 full-system simulation, measuring end-to-end latency for three distinct use cases.
key_novelty: Hardware safepoints that enable user-level runtime preemption without kernel involvement, combined with interrupt forwarding to accelerators, all built on an extended user-interrupt model.
contributions: Detailed analysis and timing model of Intel UIPI's current design and its limitations
Four hardware extensions to UIPI: tracked interrupts, hardware safepoints, kernel-bypass timer, interrupt forwarding
gem5-based modeling and evaluation across three use cases (user-level runtime preemption, DPDK IO notification, streaming accelerator notification)
Demonstrated performance matching shared-memory polling with the efficiency of asynchronous notification

metrics.other: performance of shared-memory polling with efficiency of asynchronous notification

limitations: Evaluation is gem5 simulation only; real hardware silicon validation is not performed.
primary_theme: hardware extensions for fast user-space interrupt notification without polling
